newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: MOTOR RACING-ITALY'S NANNINI SAYS F1 COMEBACK UNLIKELY.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ITALY'S NANNINI SAYS F1 COMEBACK UNLIKELY.

text.p: Alessandro Nannini, who will test a Benetton-Renault next month, said on Wednesday it was highly unlikely he would ever make a comeback to Formula One racing.

The Italian, whose F1 career came to an abrupt end in October 1990 when his right arm was severed in a helicopter accident, also denied rumours that Benetton boss Flavio Briatore would hire him as a test driver.
"I don't think my body could physically manage to complete the full distance of an F1 race," Nannini, on a promotional tour in Vienna, told a news conference.
Nevertheless, the 37-year-old Nannini, who won one F1 race in his career, will be testing the Benetton at the Estoril race track in Portugal from November 25 to 28.
Nannini currently drives an Alfa Romeo in the International Touring Car series although the movement in his right arm, which was sewn back on after the near-fatal accident, is limited.
